subject: Fix a minimum value for G parameter in 3PL

messages.author: 2c38ab32c3b498d5
messages.subject: Fix a minimum value for G parameter in 3PL
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to "reverse engineer" a score calculated using the 3PL model.

I get an overall R² of 0.987 when fitting an lm between the estimated person scores and the actual ones, specially for higher scores. However, for lower scores things get a little messed up. My guess is that this could be caused by some tweeking on the 'g' parameter, which would affect primary lower scores.

This score is calculated for a dichotomous test with 5 alternatives each question, so I suspect the minimum value for the g parameter would be 0.2. I was able to set a fixed g value using pars, but I would like to know if I could set a minimum value for estimation.

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fix a minimum value for G parameter in 3PL
parts:
Hi Eduardo,

Indeed this is possible, but for some reason I haven't added a syntax wrapper to mirt.model() yet to easily do this. I'll try to push this to the dev version for the next release next chance I get. 

For now, you can set the lower bound values manually by modifying the data frame of starting values

```
dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod <- mirt(dat, 1, '3PL') #unconstrained
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)

sv <- mirt(dat, 1, '3PL', pars = 'values') #starting values
sv$lbound[sv$name == 'g'] <- qlogis(.2)  #must be in logit units due to internal transformation

mod2 <- mirt(dat, 1, '3PL', pars=sv)
coef(mod2, simplify=TRUE)
```

This will be much easier in the next version for sure. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Fix a minimum value for G parameter in 3PL
parts:
Okay, this has been pushed to the dev version 1.9.3. It can now be run with the following

```
library(mirt)
dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
model <- 'F = 1-5
                LBOUND = (1-5, g, 0.2)'
mod <- mirt(dat, model, '3PL')
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)
```

Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fix a minimum value for G parameter in 3PL
parts:
Okay, the dev version contains the fix now. Apparently the L-BFGS-B algorithm doesn't need finite bounds anymore (neither does the nlminb optimizer), so after removing that piece of code the algorithm runs okay: 

```
library(mirt)

dat <- read.csv('~/Downloads/set100k.csv', header=TRUE)
items <- subset(dat, select = 4:ncol(dat))

large <- mirt(items, 1, large=TRUE)
mod <- mirt(items, 1, '3PL', large=large, TOL = .003) #works fine, though doesn't quite converge
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)

model <- 'theta = 1-45
LBOUND = (1-45, g, 0.2)'

mod2 <- mirt(items, model, '3PL', large=large, TOL = .003)
coef(mod2, simplify=TRUE)

mod3 <- mirt(items, model, '3PL', large=large, TOL = .003, optimizer = 'nlminb')
coef(mod3, simplify=TRUE)

colMeans(items)
```

You'll notice that some of the intercepts for some items are really large, and that's very reasonable given the data. When the guessing parameter is larger than the proportion of individuals who actually answered the item correctly the intercept becomes basically non-estimable (the response answers are pure chance, so an intercept is meaningless). It might be good to set the upper bound for the g parameter to be less than the observed proportion of correct answers, just so that the solution doesn't become all wacky. Cheers.

Phil
